summary: The note is a Wikipedia-derived overview of Colombo, the commercial capital and largest city of Sri Lanka, located on the island's west coast. It describes the city's population figures, its role as the island's financial centre and tourist destination, and its relationship to the neighbouring legislative capital Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte. It also notes its administrative roles and that it was the legislative capital until 1982.
one_line: Overview of Colombo, Sri Lanka's largest city and commercial capital, its population, administrative roles, and relation to Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte.
key_facts: Colombo is the commercial capital and largest city of Sri Lanka.
According to the Brookings Institution, the Colombo metropolitan area has a population of 5.6 million.
The city proper of Colombo has a population of 752,993.
Colombo is the financial centre of the island and a popular tourist destination.
Colombo is located on the west coast of the island of Sri Lanka.
Colombo is adjacent to the Greater Colombo area, which includes Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte and Dehiwala - Mount Lavinia.
Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is the legislative capital of Sri Lanka.
Colombo is often referred to as the capital because Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is within the urban area of, and a suburb of, Colombo.
Colombo is the administrative capital of Western Province, Sri Lanka.
Colombo is the district capital of Colombo District.
Colombo has a mixture of modern life and colonial buildings and ruins.
Colombo was the legislative capital of Sri Lanka until 1982.
